brief.headline: HBM supercycle intact—DRAM +63% Q2, hyperscaler capex $700B+, CoWoS tight through H1'27
brief.summary: <cite index="20-1,20-18">Conventional DRAM contract prices rose 90-95% QoQ in Q1 2026 and are projected to climb 58-63% QoQ in Q2</cite>, with <cite index="20-22">NAND flash contract prices expected to rise 70-75% QoQ in Q2 2026, outpacing DRAM for the first time</cite>. <cite index="1-1">Goldman Sachs forecasts a 4.9% DRAM supply deficit in 2026</cite>, while <cite index="24-5,24-9">the four biggest hyperscalers will spend roughly $700 billion on capital expenditures in 2026</cite>, with <cite index="20-9">$755 billion in 2026 hyperscaler capital expenditure and memory consuming approximately 30% of that total</cite>. <cite index="32-9">NVIDIA reportedly secured over 60% of total CoWoS capacity for 2025 and 2026</cite>, while <cite index="33-2,33-6">TSMC's entire CoWoS lineup is fully booked through orders from NVIDIA, Google, Amazon, and MediaTek</cite>. <cite index="4-6,4-7">SK Hynix announced mass shipments of sixth-generation HBM4 memory in March 2026, with all 2026 HBM production capacity sold out under binding agreements</cite>.
brief.pair_trade_view: <cite index="41-8">SK Hynix held 53% HBM market share in Q3 2025 versus Samsung's 35%</cite>, but <cite index="4-1,4-2">Micron's Seoul HBM design hiring push and Samsung's union-driven talent retention pressure signal structural engineering risk for Samsung</cite>. <cite index="42-14">Korea Investment & Securities set targets of 570,000 won for Samsung and 3.8 million won for SK Hynix</cite>, while <cite index="40-9,40-10">Nomura argued Samsung and SK Hynix should trade at 20x forward P/E similar to TSMC, versus current 7x and 6.56x multiples</cite>. <cite index="7-2">Nanya Tech GM stated DRAM margins across all segments currently outperform HBM</cite>, creating legacy DRAM pricing power that benefits Samsung's diversified portfolio. <cite index="39-20,42-17">Samsung closed at 299,500 won (+8.51%) and SK Hynix at 1.94M won (+11.17%) on May 21</cite>. Near-term edge to SK Hynix on HBM4 ramp execution and Nvidia qualification lead; Samsung trades at steeper discount to fair value with upside optionality if HBM4 customer wins materialize in H2.

memory_cycle.notes: <cite index="20-3,20-5,20-6">Structural shift driven by AI infrastructure demand creating sustained high-margin competition for capacity, with memory producers prioritizing HBM production over conventional DRAM as long as AI buildouts continue</cite>. <cite index="20-16">New fab capacity not expected to reach meaningful production volume before late 2027 or 2028</cite>. <cite index="8-9">AI will consume 20% of total DRAM production in 2026</cite>, while <cite index="8-4">producing 1 bit of HBM consumes approximately 300% the wafer capacity required for 1 bit of DDR5</cite>. <cite index="18-6,18-7,18-17">PC DRAM contract price momentum slowed in April 2026 as high costs weakened PC sales and ended extreme seller's market</cite>, suggesting early signs of demand destruction at consumer end even as server/HBM remain sold out.

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="4-6,4-7">SK Hynix began mass shipments of HBM4 (36GB, 12-high stack, 2.8 TB/s bandwidth) in March 2026 for Nvidia Vera Rubin, with all 2026 HBM capacity sold out</cite>. <cite index="4-9">Micron CEO projects global HBM market will grow from $35B in 2025 to $100B by 2028</cite>. <cite index="3-1,3-6">Intel's Crescent Island AI GPU uses LPDDR5X rather than HBM to sidestep global HBM shortage</cite>, while <cite index="10-2,10-3">Intel/SoftBank ZAM 3D stacked DRAM promises 2-3x HBM3 bandwidth at lower cost/energy</cite>. <cite index="4-1,4-10">Micron launched Seoul-based HBM design engineer recruitment targeting Samsung engineers, with largest concentration of qualified HBM circuit engineers working in Seoul</cite>. <cite index="6-1">SK Hynix is shifting Cheongju campus toward wafer testing to address HBM back-end pressure</cite>. Supply remains structural bottleneck through 2026; alternative architectures (ZAM, LPDDR5X workarounds) gaining traction for 2027+ but HBM3E/4 oligopoly pricing power intact near-term.

news_pulse.headline: DRAM Q2 contract prices +58-63% QoQ after record Q1 +90-95%; NAND +70-75% outpaces DRAM
news_pulse.implication: Sequential deceleration in DRAM pricing from Q1 extreme but still historic by absolute standards; NAND acceleration reflects enterprise SSD demand surge for AI inference KV cache storage. Supplier pricing power remains structurally intact through H1'27.

news_pulse.headline: Goldman: 4.9% DRAM supply deficit 2026; hyperscalers $700B capex (30% memory allocation)
news_pulse.implication: Persistent undersupply mathematically locks in elevated ASPs through 2026. Hyperscaler capex intensity ($700B vs $200B in 2024) confirms AI infrastructure arms race shows no deceleration; memory remains 30% of capex, translating to $210B+ direct memory spend.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix HBM4 (36GB, 12-hi, 2.8TB/s) mass production; all 2026 capacity sold out
news_pulse.implication: SK Hynix executing on HBM4 ramp ahead of Samsung, with Nvidia Vera Rubin qualification locked. Sold-out 2026 capacity eliminates spot market elasticity; any Samsung HBM4 wins would be 2027 revenue events.

news_pulse.headline: Micron recruits Seoul-based HBM engineers; Samsung talent retention under structural pressure
news_pulse.implication: Engineering talent war escalating in Seoul HBM ecosystem. Micron offering Principal-level comp approaching Samsung bonus dispute levels; Samsung union cited engineers leaving for SK Hynix and US firms. Non-compete enforcement risk but Samsung retention fragility now visible.

news_pulse.headline: TSMC CoWoS-L/S fully booked; Nvidia holds >60% capacity allocation through 2026
news_pulse.implication: Advanced packaging remains gating constraint for AI accelerator shipments. Nvidia's 60%+ allocation locks competitors (AMD, hyperscaler custom silicon) into capacity bidding wars or OSAT alternatives with inferior yields. No relief until TSMC AP7/AP8 ramps in H2'26-H1'27.

news_pulse.headline: Nanya Tech GM: legacy DRAM margins now outperform HBM; DDR4 3-year supply contracts
news_pulse.implication: Counter-narrative to HBM-only thesis: legacy DRAM scarcity (Samsung/SK cutting DDR4 for HBM reallocation) drives margin expansion across commodity segments. Supports Samsung's diversified portfolio positioning; pure-play HBM exposure (SK Hynix) faces margin pressure if legacy DRAM pricing peaks.

news_pulse.headline: KOSPI +606pts (8.42%) record surge; Samsung/SK Hynix combined mkt cap ₩3,133T (49% KOSPI)
news_pulse.implication: Retail euphoria at peak levels; 24-25% of existing Samsung/SK holders added positions in March rally. Nomura raised KOSPI target to 10,000-11,000 on HBM supercycle thesis. Crowding risk elevated; any HBM qualification delays or hyperscaler capex guide-downs would trigger violent unwind.

news_pulse.headline: 18 single-stock leveraged/inverse Samsung & SK Hynix ETFs/ETNs list May 27 (₩43.2T size)
news_pulse.implication: Retail leverage products launching into parabolic rally signals froth. ₩43.2T planned listing size amplifies both momentum and reversal risk. Derivatives launch historically coincides with near-term vol spikes; watch for gamma-driven intraday swings post-listing.

brief.derivatives_signal: Extreme bullish positioning into May 27 leveraged ETF/ETN launch (₩43.2T); gamma risk and retail crowding at cycle highs. Options OI skew likely reflects call overweight. Near-term tactical fade on any incremental negative HBM news (Samsung qualification delay, hyperscaler capex cut) would be violent given leverage embedded in new products and 49% index concentration. Structurally long memory into H1'27 but setup for 10-15% consolidation before next leg.
